question: If cotA = x + ((1)/(x)), then what is cosec²A?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The standard trigonometric identity is cosec²A = 1 + cot²A.

Substitute cotA = x + (1/x) directly into the formula.

cosec²A = 1 + [x + (1/x)]²

cosec²A = 1 + x² + (1/x²) + 2

cosec²A = x² + (1/x²) + 3

**∴ The correct answer is x² + (1/x²) + 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cotA = x + (1/x)

**Formula Used:**

cosec²A − cot²A = 1

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ cosec²A = 1 + cot²A

⇒ cosec²A = 1 + [x + (1/x)]²

⇒ cosec²A = 1 + x² + (1/x)² + 2 × x × (1/x)

⇒ cosec²A = 1 + x² + (1/x²) + 2

⇒ cosec²A = x² + (1/x²) + 3

**∴ The correct answer is x² + (1/x²) + 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Trigonometric Identities

• sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

• sec²θ − tan²θ = 1

• cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

Reciprocal Trigonometric Identities

• sinθ = 1 ÷ cosecθ

• cosθ = 1 ÷ secθ

• tanθ = 1 ÷ cotθ

Standard Algebraic Identity

• (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab
